_doc: Source of truth for the ledger's Research map and docs/research/RESEARCH-MAP.md (built by scripts/build_research_map.py). One entry per item; an item lists every theme it belongs to, so a cross-cutting experiment shows up under each. kind: finding | experiment | idea | fix | check | design | literature. status: done | running | next (proposed for the next round) | planned | gated | parked | dropped | untouched (never started). grade (findings): A strong and replicated | B solid, one gap | C suggestive | D weak or explanation-level | N settled negative. ev: ledger anchors. src: where the item comes from (paper key, 'ours', a doc, or the chat). Updated 2026-10-14.

themes.title: Are the numbers right? Benchmark and measurement validity
themes.question: Which measured differences are pipeline, labelling or scoring artefacts rather than properties of the script or the model?
themes.summary: The strongest results are here. Loose KHATT crops cost fixed-height models 7.5 CER points, and an old length filter hid the worst of them. Hamza and digit conventions differ between label sets, and even between NAKBA's two test splits. KHATT labels carry spacing quirks. 11 % of NAKBA blind lines repeat training text and are memorised by NAKBA-trained systems, though corpus scores barely move. A PaddleOCR flag scrambled its output; kitab_muharaf is mostly Muharaf train. The per-line store, page-cluster intervals and the corrections log now guard every number. Open: label-noise rate and human readability (needs review), near-duplicates, the diacritic scoring rule.

themes.title: Connectivity, PAWs and word spacing
themes.question: Does Arabic's split of words into parts (PAWs) make word boundaries ambiguous to recognisers, and is that visual?
themes.summary: Every family inserts word-internal spaces at PAW gaps far more than chance (87 of 89 pairs). Spaces cost more than dots: the space tax is 2–11 CER points against 1–4. PAWs per word was word length. Open: are split PAW gaps as wide as word gaps (pixel measurement); PAW-aware decoding; PAW tokens for a shape vocabulary.

themes.title: Dots: skeleton (rasm) against dots (i'jam)
themes.question: How much of the error is dots, at what resolution do dots get lost, and can context restore them?
themes.summary: Without dots, about nine tenths of every family's error remains: models misread skeletons, not dots, and lines that are right except for their dots are rare (0.1–4 %). Three-dot letters are the most dot-error-prone. A quarter to a third of words share their dotless form with another word, yet the most frequent word restores 95 % of known words. The dots matter for the fifth of words that are unseen, which echoes why iʿjām was invented. Confusions are visual, not phonetic. Open: a two-stage reader (skeleton recogniser plus constrained dot restorer), dot-writing styles (dash, caret, displaced), and a dot-preserving resize below 48 px.

themes.title: Letter shapes, positional forms and allographs
themes.question: Which letter shapes are hard, why, and does adding the missing shapes help?
themes.summary: Letter-shape novelty passes the confound battery (within-line OR ≈ 16 for CRNNs, 4.4 for fine-tuned VLMs); pixel novelty is weak. Shape-targeted repeats beat random on KHATT, including held-out lines, but nowhere else. The positional-form tail is covered. Since most error is skeleton misreading, the next questions are which skeleton features fail (loops, teeth, tails, vertical stacking) and the shape programme: an allograph library with joins and dots kept separate, synthesis from it, and shape-token recognition with a constrained decoder. Feasibility: CTC spans are anchors, not cut lines, and handwritten PAWs often touch, so extraction needs alignment and ink together.

themes.title: Script styles and transcription conventions
themes.question: How do style conventions (Maghrebi dots, hamza writing) change what models must learn, and how fast can they learn them?
themes.summary: Maghrebi qāf/fāʾ convention (base AIN 23–27 % ق→ف). Without Maghrebi training a CRNN reads RASAM at ~47 % CER instead of ~12 %. Hamza use follows the training labels. Writers spell as they speak (Levantine متل for مثل in Muharaf labels). Open: a few-shot Maghrebi curve, dot-swap augmentation, the style inventory.

themes.title: Writing geometry and image conditions
themes.question: Which geometric and image properties (crop, slant, stroke, resolution, rules, tone) change recognition, and for which model families?
themes.summary: Ink crop: −7.5 points on KHATT for every CRNN. Slant is causal but small, and slant TTA gated on measured slant is nearly free. Slant/stroke augmentation hurts on unseen sets. Tone, noise and ruled lines: no effect. Jointly, pixels per character and line length predict errors in every family; loose crops and slant only for CRNNs. Open: normalisation ablation (height, padding, deslant), resolution probe, a VLM check on crop and slant.

themes.title: Language and text: what the decoder knows
themes.question: How much of the gap is text distance (unseen words, register), and can a language prior help without hallucinating?
themes.summary: Unseen words hurt every family. KHATT text is the farthest from training. An unconstrained LLM decoder hurts (E8). Errors are visual. Without dots, context restores 95 % of known words but not unseen ones, so a language prior helps only under the image's constraint. Open: constrained decoding with character language models and a comprehensive lexicon (words, names, places), and synthesis from any text.

themes.title: Writers and hands
themes.question: How much of line difficulty is the writer, and do the effects hold within writers?
themes.summary: Writers can now be studied. RASAM-2 has 15 manuscripts of 24–31 lines, RASAM-1 three large ones, and NAKBA is one writer. Page-cluster intervals were added; they match line intervals because seed noise dominates. The full KHATT v1.0 (1,038 test lines) is downloaded, but has no writer IDs. Next: writer adaptation, both for the CRNN (few lines chosen to cover the letters) and for VLMs in context (a labelled reference line in the same prompt), and a calibration sentence covering every letter form.

themes.title: Models, training data and transfer
themes.question: What transfers across datasets and model families, and what is a fair reference?
themes.summary: CRNN and VLM difficulty correlate weakly, and the per-line better of the two is far below either: KHATT 14.3 % against 17.4 / 18.1 %, NAKBA test 4.1 % against 10.2 / 18.7 %. So a cross-family combination is a strong candidate. The standard-split CRNN is the comparable reference. Repetition helps NAKBA slightly. Open: in-domain NAKBA and KHATT controls, the combination, E1, the multilingual freeze sweep, data scaling, the cross-script check.

themes.title: Attribution and localisation: where models look
themes.question: Do models look at the right letters, and can attribution guide training?
themes.summary: Attribution maps are valid (9× on ink) and point at the token's own letters about 3× chance. Wrong tokens look in the right place as often as correct ones, so errors are misreadings, not misdirected looking. LocateAnything zero-shot failed. Open, and parked behind the characterisation work: image reliance, dots, per-module gradients, freeze-by-letter.

themes.title: Our own dataset (design)
themes.question: What would a dataset that answers these questions look like?
themes.summary: A living design guide exists (dataset-design.md). Findings feed it: size in characters per letter × form, writer metadata, a tight crop policy, a documented hamza and diacritic convention, shared copy-texts across writers.

themes.title: Infrastructure, standards and literature
themes.question: How do we make every result traceable and every characteristic reusable?
themes.summary: Built: store, panel, seeds, analyses A and B, 18 detectors, page-cluster intervals, corrections log, research map with coverage check, SSD backups. Open: correction for multiple comparisons; reporting in WER and lines fixed; decision rules, dependencies and a claims register per item; gates V3–V6; items that need the main checkout (PaddleOCR patch, NEXT_STEPS, Atlas tracker).
